meta.mechanism: ATP citrate lyase inhibitor (liver-activated prodrug; acts upstream of HMG-CoA reductase)
meta.indication: reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in statin-intolerant patients with, or at high risk for, cardiovascular disease (primary and secondary prevention)

n_randomized.quote: A total of 13,970 patients underwent randomization; 6992 were assigned to the bempedoic acid group and 6978 to the placebo group.
n_randomized.note: Registry (S3) actual enrollment also 13970. Design paper (S4, Oct 2020) said 14,014 randomized - see open_questions.

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up was 40.6 months.

primary_endpoint.value: Time to first MACE-4: death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary end point was a four-component composite of major adverse cardiovascular events, defined as death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization.
primary_endpoint.note: Hospitalization for unstable angina was removed from the primary composite by amendment (S1 Statistical Analysis).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age 18-85; previous CV event or high CV risk; patient-reported statin intolerance (unable/unwilling to take statins due to adverse effects), very-low-dose statin allowed; LDL-C >=100 mg/dL on maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy; 4-week single-blind placebo run-in
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients 18 to 85 years of age were eligible if they met either of two criteria for increased cardiovascular risk — a previous cardiovascular event (secondary-prevention patients) or clinical features that placed them at high risk for a cardiovascular event (primary-prevention patients).
inclusion_key_criteria.note: LDL-C >=100 mg/dL criterion quoted from design paper abstract (S4): 'an LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL on maximally-tolerated lipid-lowering therapy'.

planned_events.quote: For the trial to have 90% power, a minimum of 1620 primary end-point events were required to have occurred.
planned_events.note: Also required: at least 810 key secondary (MACE-3) events and >=24 months follow-up of all patients. Design paper S4 also states 1620. Observed primary events: 819+927=1746.

assumed_rrr.quote: This event-driven trial was designed to provide at least 90% power to detect a 15% reduction in the relative risk of a primary end-point event at an overall two-sided significance level of 0.05.

power.quote: This event-driven trial was designed to provide at least 90% power to detect a 15% reduction in the relative risk of a primary end-point event

alpha.quote: at an overall two-sided significance level of 0.05
alpha.note: Hierarchical testing of primary then six key secondary end points; no interim efficacy analyses.

stopped_early.quote: No interim efficacy analyses were conducted.
stopped_early.note: Trial ran to completion (registry primary completion 2022-11-07). Ukraine sites censored after 2022-02-24.

genetics.finding: Genetic scores in ACLY (mimicking ATP citrate lyase inhibition) and HMGCR (mimicking statins) produced similar lipid/lipoprotein changes and similar CV risk reduction per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C; no increase in cancer.
genetics.effect: OR 0.823 (95% CI 0.78-0.87) for CV events per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C (ACLY score) vs OR 0.836 (0.81-0.87) for HMGCR score; 654,783 participants, 105,429 with major CV events
genetics.quote: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.823 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.87; P = 4.0×10-14) for the ACLY score and 0.836 (95% CI, 0.81 to 0.87; P = 3.9×10-19) for the HMGCR score.
genetics.note: Published BEFORE the CLEAR Outcomes readout (2022-12-07). Funded in part by Esperion ('Funded by Esperion Therapeutics and others'). Implies benefit is proportional to absolute LDL-C lowering, so a ~20-30 mg/dL reduction predicts a modest (~13-18%) RRR.

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal for ASCVD; ACLY-mediated LDL-C lowering has the same per-unit effect as HMGCR-mediated lowering (same source). No separate LDL-C MR source curated for this case.
genetics.quote: Genetic variants that mimic the effect of ATP citrate lyase inhibitors and statins appeared to lower plasma LDL cholesterol levels by the same mechanism of action and were associated with similar effects on the risk of cardiovascular disease per unit decrease in the LDL cholesterol level.
genetics.note: hsCRP lowering by bempedoic acid is not considered causal (see CRP MR, CCGC 2011 BMJ, curated in cantos.json).

consensus_explanation.summary: Bempedoic acid met its MACE-4 primary endpoint (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.79-0.96) in statin-intolerant patients. The 13% relative risk reduction is modest and is consistent with the size of LDL-C lowering (about 29 mg/dL at 6 months, about 22 mg/dL time-averaged) as predicted by CTT meta-analysis and by ACLY Mendelian randomization (same per-unit LDL-C benefit as statins). Nuances: (1) the trial was sized to detect a 15% RRR with 1620 events, so it was powered for a modest effect, and the observed effect landed close to that assumption; (2) the primary endpoint included coronary revascularization; MI and revascularization drove the benefit, while CV death, all-cause death and stroke were not significantly reduced; (3) the population had a high baseline LDL-C (139 mg/dL) because statins were largely absent, which increased the absolute LDL-C reduction; (4) bempedoic acid also lowered hsCRP by about 22% (not considered causal); (5) the safety cost is gout, hyperuricemia and cholelithiasis. The FDA expanded the label to CV risk reduction (announced 2024-03-22).
